name: flex_connect_solar
description: A 5 MW electrically driven aqueous process on a PG&E Flex Connect service with 1 MW of on-site solar. The process runs at 80-100% of rated whenever it is on, cannot change state for less than an hour, and must average 95% of rated over the week. Flex Connect caps grid import hour by hour, a day ahead, and tightens that cap in the hours the local transmission constraint is congested -- which in PG&E in 2025 were the solar hours.

time._comment: One summer week at 15-minute resolution, in local (Pacific) clock time. The solar resource is a GFS forecast initialized at weather.init_utc, converted to this clock.

process._comment: A ConstantEnergyIntensityModel: power = energy_intensity * outlet flow. Rated flow is derived, rated_power_kw / energy_intensity_kwh_per_m3. When on it runs anywhere in [min_load_fraction, 1] of rated; min_up_hours / min_down_hours are converted to steps of time_step_hours. utilization_target is the horizon-average output as a fraction of rated, enforced on the product boundary's total delivery.

solar._comment: A GenericRenewables unit whose capacity factor comes from hefty: a GFS solar resource forecast run through hefty.pv_model.model_pv_power for a single-axis tracker. capacity_factor = AC output / nameplate_ac_kw.

weather._comment: hefty.solar.get_solar_forecast arguments. GFS is global, so a free lat/lon in notebook.py works too. lead_time_to_start is chosen by sites.py so the forecast starts at the horizon's local midnight. priority 'dynamical' reads GFS from dynamical.org's Zarr archive (needs dynamical_catalog and cartopy); drop it to download GRIB from NOAA's AWS bucket instead, which is much slower.

flex_connect._comment: Synthetic PG&E Flex Connect day-ahead hourly import limits. The service is sized at service_kw, and in a share of hours equal to the site's historical congestion_share (sites.json) the cap drops to curtailed_kw. Those hours are drawn from the constraint's binding window, nearest midday first, spread across the week. Export is not allowed (load-only Flex Connect).

tariff._comment: A PG&E B-20 (secondary) shaped summer tariff as EECO rate rows: a monthly customer charge, a max-demand charge over all hours, a peak-period demand charge, and three TOU energy periods (peak 16-21, part-peak 14-16 and 21-23, off-peak otherwise). The numbers are representative of B-20 secondary summer rates, rounded, not a quote of the current tariff book. Demand charges are monthly and are applied to this one-week horizon as-is, the same simplification pump_scheduling makes.
